title: Xi Jinping Is Coming to the US. Why Is He Skipping the UNGA?
author: Shannon Tiezzi
text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping addresses the general debate of the General Assembly’s 70th session, Sep. 28, 2015. That was the first and only time Xi attended a session of the UNGA in person.
Credit: UN Photo/Cia Pak
If you read The Diplomat, you probably follow Asia-Pacific affairs – and thus you probably already know that Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to arrive in Washington, D.C. today for a much-anticipated summit with U.S. President Donald Trump.According to the White House’s itinerary, Xi will land at Andrews Air Force Base on September 23, where he will be personally received by Trump himself. The next day, he’ll receive a formal welcome ceremony at the White House, followed by the actual summit and a state dinner. On September 25, Trump and First Lady Melania Trump will host Xi and his wife for tea; both couples will then visit the National Archives, “where they will view a variety of important records and documents significant to the American and Chinese relationship throughout history.” Then Xi and his delegation will fly home.[...]
